# Surface accuracy and data efficiency: DrivAerML Surface and HiLiftAeroML {#sec-surface}

```{python}
#| label: setup-surface
#| include: false
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from palette import *
import json, statistics
from pathlib import Path
RES = Path("..") / "results"
J = lambda p: json.load(open(RES / p))
mean = statistics.mean
pct = lambda r: f"{abs(1 - r) * 100:.0f}%"

# DrivAerML Surface task: the five rungs of the training-car ladder
P2 = J("p200k_trio_reduction_2026-09-19.json"); L2 = J("p200k_ladder_interim_2026-09-18.json")
def ladder_rung(n):
    r = L2["rungs"][n]
    gt = {"1e-3": r["gt_unit"], "3e-3": r["rate_control_lr3e3"]["gt_unit_lr3e3"]}
    glab = min(gt, key=lambda k: gt[k]["pressure_mean"])
    seeds = lambda a: [v["pressure_l2"] for v in a["per_seed"].values()]
    return dict(isla=seeds(r["isla"]), gt=seeds(gt[glab]), gt_rate=glab, t=seeds(r["transolver_unit"]))
A = P2["arms"]
gt435 = {"1e-3": A["gt_unit_lr1e3"], "3e-3": A["gt_unit_lr3e3"]}
g435lab = min(gt435, key=lambda k: gt435[k]["pressure_mean"])
runs = lambda a: [v["pressure_l2"] for v in a["per_run"].values()]
CARS = {int(n[1:]): ladder_rung(n) for n in ("n27", "n54", "n109", "n218")}
CARS[435] = dict(isla=runs(A["isla"]), gt=runs(gt435[g435lab]), gt_rate=g435lab, t=runs(A["transolver_unit_lr3e3"]))
car_ratio = {n: (mean(r["gt"]) / mean(r["isla"]), mean(r["t"]) / mean(r["isla"])) for n, r in CARS.items()}
ISO = J("isocost_reduction_2026-09-20.json")["configurations"]
iso_pair = ISO["gt_unit|w256|c200k|lr3e-3|ep500"]["pressure_l2_mean"] / ISO["isla|w192|c200k|lr1e-3|ep500"]["pressure_l2_mean"]

# HiLiftAeroML: the case ladder, the geometry ladder and the fixed-angle split
F19 = J("p200k_fleet_reduction_2026-09-19.json")["datasets"]
F20 = J("p200k_fleet_interim_2026-09-20.json")["datasets"]
F22 = J("p200k_fleet_reduction_2026-09-22.json")["datasets"]
RN = J("routenorm_p200k_2026-09-22.json")
def gt_best(d):
    """GeoTransolver at the better of its 1e-3 and 3e-3 pairs; the rate label is read from the arm names,
    and 'rate not recorded' is printed where the artifact holds a single GeoTransolver arm without one."""
    a = d["arms"]; cands = {k: a[k] for k in ("gt_unit", "gt_unit_lr3e3") if k in a and a[k].get("n_evaluated")}
    k = min(cands, key=lambda k: cands[k]["pressure_l2_mean"])
    if len(cands) == 2:
        lab = "3e-3" if k.endswith("lr3e3") else "1e-3"
    else:
        lab = "3e-3" if k.endswith("lr3e3") else "rate not recorded"
    return cands[k]["pressure_l2_seeds"], lab
def wing_rung(d, isla=None):
    g, lab = gt_best(d)
    return dict(gt=g, gt_rate=lab, t=d["arms"]["transolver_unit"]["pressure_l2_seeds"],
                isla=isla if isla is not None else d["arms"]["isla"]["pressure_l2_seeds"])
COS192 = RN["configurations"]["wings35|cos|w192|lr1e-3|c200k"]["pressure_l2_seeds"]
COS384 = RN["configurations"]["wings35|cos|w384|lr1e-3|c200k"]
WINGS = {
 "35 training cases": wing_rung(F19["highlift_surface_super_scarce"], isla=COS192),
 "210 training cases": wing_rung(F22["highlift_surface_scarce"]),
 "4 training geometries": wing_rung(F20["highlift_surface_geometry_super_scarce"]),
 "21 training geometries": wing_rung(F22["highlift_surface_geometry_scarce"]),
 "126 geometries at 12°": wing_rung(F20["highlift_surface_single_aoa_12"]),
}
wing_ratio = {k: (mean(r["gt"]) / mean(r["isla"]), mean(r["t"]) / mean(r["isla"])) for k, r in WINGS.items()}
```

```{python}
#| label: para-surface-lede
#| output: asis
g27, g435 = car_ratio[27][0], car_ratio[435][0]
w = wing_ratio
print(f"**On the DrivAerML Surface task ISLA and GeoTransolver are at parity at full data (GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA {g435:.3f} at 435 "
      f"training cars, within the seed spread) and ISLA leads Transolver by {pct(car_ratio[435][1])}; below full data GeoTransolver holds a "
      f"data-efficiency lead that narrows from {pct(g27)} at 27 cars to zero at 435. On HiLiftAeroML the baselines lead ISLA on every rung: "
      f"GeoTransolver by {pct(w['35 training cases'][0])} at 35 training cases, {pct(w['4 training geometries'][0])} at 4 training geometries "
      f"and {pct(w['126 geometries at 12°'][0])} on the fixed-angle split, by {pct(w['210 training cases'][0])} at 210 cases and by "
      f"{pct(w['21 training geometries'][0])} where the validation geometries are never seen at 21 training geometries.** "
      "The wing deficit is a small-data, recurring-geometry effect: it shrinks with training cases, is within seed noise where the "
      "validation geometries are held out of a training set of a few tens of geometries, and does not move with the number of sampled "
      "cells. The metric throughout is the area-weighted relative L2 error of surface pressure in float32 (@sec-metrics); every ratio is "
      "baseline ÷ ISLA, above one favoring ISLA; protocol: @sec-protocol (200,000 sampled cells per case, 500 epochs, two seeds, each "
      "architecture at its own best learning rate, parameters matched at ISLA 8.9M, GeoTransolver 9.0M, Transolver 6.0M).")
```

for n, r in CARS.items():
    b = "**" if n == 435 else ""
    out += (f"| {b}{n}{b} | {b}{cell(r['isla'])}{b} | {b}{cell(r['gt'])}{b} ({r['gt_rate']}) | {b}{cell(r['t'])}{b} "
            f"| {b}{car_ratio[n][0]:.2f}{b} | {b}{car_ratio[n][1]:.2f}{b} |\n")
print(out)
print(": Surface-pressure error on the DrivAerML Surface task (area-weighted relative L2, float32, 48 validation cars): seed mean "
      "(seed range) with every model trained and scored at 200,000 sampled cells per case, width 192 (ISLA) and 256 (GeoTransolver, "
      "Transolver), 500 epochs, two seeds. GeoTransolver's column takes the better of its 1e-3 and 3e-3 pairs and names the rate. "
      "How to read this: ratios above 1 favor ISLA; the 435-car row is the full training split and the book's primary standing on this "
      "task. Data: results/p200k_trio_reduction_2026-09-19.json; results/p200k_ladder_interim_2026-09-18.json. {#tbl-scoreboard-200k}")

      "200,000-cell protocol is a converged budget on this task.")

### The anatomy of the cell-count gap {#sec-deficit-anatomy}

```{python}
#| label: para-anatomy-200k
#| output: asis
tenk = P2["tenk_reference"]
qv = J("quadvar_reduction_2026-09-17.json")["arms"]
r_ind10 = qv["gt_unit"]["unif"]["10000"] / qv["isla_ref"]["unif"]["10000"]
r_strat10 = qv["gt_unit"]["strat"]["10000"]["mean"] / qv["isla_ref"]["strat"]["10000"]["mean"]
r_ind40 = qv["gt_unit"]["unif"]["40000"] / qv["isla_ref"]["unif"]["40000"]
r435 = CARS[435]
print(f"**Below 100,000 cells per case ISLA's error carries finite-sample noise in its slice integrals, and at the reporting protocol it is "
      f"gone.** The cell-count ladder makes the term visible: trained and scored at 10,000 cells (a rung of the ladder, not a standing) "
      f"GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA is {tenk['gt_unit'] / tenk['isla']:.2f}; at 200,000 cells it is {g435:.3f}. Every model improves with the "
      f"denser sample, ISLA by the most ({(1 - P2['verdict']['isla_200k_over_10k']) * 100:.0f}% against "
      f"{(1 - mean(r435['gt']) / tenk['gt_unit']) * 100:.0f}% for GeoTransolver and {(1 - mean(r435['t']) / tenk['transolver_unit']) * 100:.0f}% for "
      "Transolver). An independent draw of a car's surface at a small cell count is a noisy instrument, and ISLA's slice states, being "
      "measure-weighted means over the draw (@sec-isla-quadrature), inherit more of that noise than the baselines' unweighted aggregates. "
      f"Two readings of the same 435-car checkpoints locate it: a stratified draw of the same 10,000 cells (@sec-using-sampler), which keeps "
      f"the inclusion law and spreads the cells evenly, moves GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA from {r_ind10:.3f} to {r_strat10:.3f}; an independent "
      f"40,000-cell draw moves it to {r_ind40:.3f}; at 200,000 cells it is {g435:.3f}. For deployment the consequence is the recommendation "
      "of @sec-using-sampler: use the stratified draw, or more cells. The wing deficit below is a different mechanism, and the cell count "
      "does not touch it. Data: results/p200k_trio_reduction_2026-09-19.json (with its 10,000-cell reference), "
      "results/quadvar_reduction_2026-09-17.json.")
```

## HiLiftAeroML {#sec-data-efficiency}

### What is measured {#sec-de-setup}

HiLiftAeroML (@sec-datasets) holds 1,800 cases: 180 high-lift wing
geometries, each simulated at ten angles of attack from 4° to 22°. Three
ladders vary what the training set contains and how large it is; all of
them score on 180 validation cases with the same instrument.

- **The case ladder.** Nested random draws of 35 and 210 training cases
  from a 1,260-case pool, sharing one 180-case validation set
  (@sec-splits). The validation geometries recur in training at other
  angles. The 35-case draw contains 33 distinct geometries and no case at
  18°.
- **The geometry ladder.** 40 cases on 4 geometries and 210 cases on 21
  geometries, each at all ten angles, validated on 180 cases of 18
  geometries that appear in no training set.
- **The fixed-angle split.** 126 geometries at 12°, validated on 18
  held-out geometries at the same angle.

Protocol: @sec-protocol. GeoTransolver's better rate on the wings is 3e-3
wherever both of its pairs exist; Transolver runs at 3e-3 and ISLA at 1e-3.

### The ladders {#sec-de-result}

```{python}
#| label: fig-hilift-data-efficiency
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The HiLiftAeroML rungs at the reporting protocol (200,000 cells per
#|   case). Surface-pressure error (area-weighted relative L2, float32, 180
#|   validation cases) on a logarithmic axis for the five rungs: 35 and 210
#|   random training cases (validation geometries recur in training at other
#|   angles); 4 and 21 training geometries at all their angles (validation
#|   geometries never seen); 126 geometries at a fixed 12° (18 held-out
#|   geometries). ISLA blue squares, GeoTransolver red circles, Transolver
#|   amber triangles; the large marker is the seed mean, the small dots the
#|   seeds; the label at the right of each row is GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA and
#|   Transolver ÷ ISLA. Where two baselines coincide their markers overlap.
#|   How to read this: the baselines' lead is largest where the training set
#|   is small and its geometries recur in validation, shrinks with cases, and
#|   is within seed noise where the validation geometries are never seen at
#|   21 training geometries; the rungs differ several-fold in absolute error,
#|   which is why the axis is logarithmic. It does not show the uncertainty
#|   from the choice of training draw, three to eleven times the seed spread
#|   at 35 cases (@sec-de-controls). Data:
#|   results/routenorm_p200k_2026-09-22.json (ISLA, 35 cases);
#|   results/p200k_fleet_reduction_2026-09-19.json (baselines, 35 cases);
#|   results/p200k_fleet_interim_2026-09-20.json (4 geometries, fixed angle);
#|   results/p200k_fleet_reduction_2026-09-22.json (210 cases, 21 geometries).
#| code-fold: true
ROWS = [("35 training cases", "35 random training cases\n(geometries recur)"),
        ("210 training cases", "210 random training cases\n(geometries recur)"),
        ("4 training geometries", "4 training geometries, 40 cases\n(never-seen geometries)"),
        ("21 training geometries", "21 training geometries, 210 cases\n(never-seen geometries)"),
        ("126 geometries at 12°", "126 geometries at a fixed 12°\n(18 held-out geometries)")]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9.6, 4.8))
ys = list(range(len(ROWS)))[::-1]
for y, (name, label) in zip(ys, ROWS):
    r = WINGS[name]
    ax.axhline(y, color=GRID, lw=0.8, zorder=0)
    for key, arm in (("gt", "gt"), ("t", "t"), ("isla_ref", "isla")):
        kw = series_kwargs(key, ls="none", ms=9)
        ax.plot([mean(r[arm])], [y], **kw, zorder=4)
        ax.plot(r[arm], [y] * len(r[arm]), ls="none", marker="o", ms=3.4, color=STYLE[key]["color"], zorder=5)
    ax.text(1.02, y, f"GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA {wing_ratio[name][0]:.2f}\nTransolver ÷ ISLA {wing_ratio[name][1]:.2f}", va="center", ha="left", fontsize=8.5, color=INK2,
            transform=ax.get_yaxis_transform())
ax.set_yticks(ys); ax.set_yticklabels([lab for _, lab in ROWS], fontsize=8.5); ax.set_ylim(-0.6, len(ROWS) - 0.4)
ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_xlim(0.015, 0.35)
ax.set_xticks([0.02, 0.03, 0.05, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.3]); ax.set_xticklabels(["0.02", "0.03", "0.05", "0.1", "0.15", "0.2", "0.3"])
ax.xaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter()); ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
ax.set_xlabel("surface-pressure relative L2 error [–], 200,000 cells per case, 180 validation cases")
h = [mpl.lines.Line2D([], [], **series_kwargs(k, ls="none", ms=8)) for k in ("isla_ref", "gt", "t")]
h.append(mpl.lines.Line2D([], [], marker="o", color=INK2, ls="none", ms=3.4, label="seeds"))
fig.legend(handles=h, loc="upper left", fontsize=8.5, ncol=4, bbox_to_anchor=(0.01, 1.0))
fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0, 0.82, 0.94))
plt.show()
```

      "within seed noise of one another once the training set holds a few tens of geometries. The preregistered bar for an ISLA advantage, "

      f"{w384['gt_over_cosine_384']:.2f}), the capacity axis @sec-shared-floor treats. The deficit is not a shortage of sampled cells: the "
      f"cell-count control trains and scores the same three architectures at 10,000 and 200,000 cells on the 35-case and fixed-angle rungs, "
      f"and GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA moves from {ctl35[1]:.2f} to {ctl35[0]:.2f} and from {fx10:.2f} to {fx:.2f} while every model on the "
      "fixed-angle rung improves by 20 to 25% (results/p200k_fleet_reduction_2026-09-19.json; results/p200k_fleet_interim_2026-09-20.json; "
      "results/fp32_reeval/fp32_shift_2026-09-09.json; results/frame_reduction_2026-09-11.json).")

### Controls {#sec-de-controls}

```{python}
#| label: para-de-controls
#| output: asis
CA = Path("..") / "research" / "transfer_program" / "studies" / "campaign_a_draws"
C35 = json.load(open(CA / "campaign_a_n35_fp32_2026-09-10.json"))["ratios"]
C210 = json.load(open(CA / "campaign_a_n210_fp32_2026-09-10.json"))["ratios"]
rng_ = lambda r: (min(v["ratio"] for v in r["per_draw"].values()), max(v["ratio"] for v in r["per_draw"].values()))
g35, t35 = rng_(C35["gt_over_isla_n35"]), rng_(C35["transolver_over_isla_n35"])
g210, t210 = C210["gt_over_isla_n210"]["ci90"], C210["transolver_over_isla_n210"]["ci90"]
print("**The two-seed spread at small rungs understates the uncertainty by a factor of three to eleven; the training draw is the larger "
      "source, and the ordering holds on every draw.** The 35-case split is one random draw from the pool. Re-training GeoTransolver, "
      "Transolver and an ISLA diagnostic configuration on three further geometry-stratified 35-case draws, three seeds each (the interval "
      f"measures the draw, not the configuration), puts GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA between {g35[0]:.2f} and {g35[1]:.2f} across the four draws "
      f"and Transolver ÷ ISLA between {t35[0]:.2f} and {t35[1]:.2f}, with the curated draw typical for every arm; at 210 cases the same design "
      f"gives 90% intervals of {g210[0]:.2f} to {g210[1]:.2f} and {t210[0]:.2f} to {t210[1]:.2f}. Every 35-case ratio in the book is to be read "
      "with a between-draw spread of this size, and the intervals exist at 35 and 210 cases only. Data: "
      "research/transfer_program/studies/campaign_a_draws/campaign_a_n35_fp32_2026-09-10.json; campaign_a_n210_fp32_2026-09-10.json.")
```

### What ISLA's error responds to {#sec-de-strata}

```{python}
#| label: para-de-strata
#| output: asis
geo_cost = mean(WINGS["4 training geometries"]["isla"]) / mean(WINGS["35 training cases"]["isla"])
print(f"**ISLA's error is paid for in geometries, not cases.** Cutting the training geometries eight-fold at a similar case count (4 "
      f"geometries at ten angles against 35 cases on 33 geometries) costs ISLA {geo_cost:.1f}x (@tbl-hilift-ladder). The comparison changes "
      "the validation population as well as the training composition, so it supports a geometry-count reading and not the stronger "
      "statement that geometry count alone sets the error.")
```

### Limits of the claims {#sec-de-limits}


- **The ladders are data-efficiency measurements, not scaling laws.** Their
  rungs span the range of data every production CFD dataset in this program
  occupies. On the DrivAerML Surface task the flattening has a measured
  cause, a shared floor of about 0.040 that both architectures reach given
  width and depth, with the cell count flat above 100,000
  (@sec-shared-floor); on the wings the flattening is not attributed.
- **Every number is in-distribution and a validation-set figure.** The
  validation cases share the training design; checkpoints are final-epoch
  with no selection, but the validation set entered more than one decision:
  each architecture's learning rate on the full split (@sec-lr-protocol),
  the baselines' rate per rung, the design of the ablations and the choice
  of what to present. No HiLiftAeroML split remains that could confirm the
  numbers independently of the program's own history: the sealed test
  splits were spent on regime extrapolation and the deflection split, which
  between them read every one of the 180 geometries
  (results/hilift_exposure_ledger_2026-09-08.json). Every remaining test
  split is therefore held out per checkpoint, since no model trained on it,
  but not a program-level confirmation; an independent confirmation needs
  geometries no part of the program has scored, which on HiLiftAeroML means
  a prospective dataset.
- **Seeds do not measure the choice of training cases.** Every seed at a
  rung trains on the same curated subset, so seed ranges measure
  initialization; the draw intervals of @sec-de-controls are the
  uncertainty to read.
- **No in-distribution ISLA accuracy advantage on the surface is
  established, so no mechanism for one is claimed.** ISLA reaches parity
  with GeoTransolver at full DrivAerML data and trails it below; on the
  wings it trails on every rung. What ISLA buys is stated with its scope
  where it is measured: exact pose covariance (@sec-pose-contract), weak
  dependence on the law the training sample is drawn by
  (@sec-training-law), slice territories that stay put under a change of
  draw (@sec-territories), the interior velocity lead on two datasets
  (@sec-interior) and the memory frontier at the scaling budget
  (@sec-shared-floor). The mechanism of the wing deficit, the mesher pattern
  where validation geometries recur in training, is an open question
  (@sec-open-questions).
- **Regime extrapolation is unmeasured for ISLA.** Across an angle-of-attack
  or stall boundary the architectures measured lose about an order of
  magnitude in error; the notebook carries the degradation ratios
  (@sec-nb-hl-sealed-test), and this chapter makes no cross-regime claim.
